name: Sacrifices
overview: Scripture reveals that sacrifices were integral from the earliest days of humanity, beginning with Cain and Abel who brought offerings from the fruit of the ground and the firstlings of their flocks, respectively, with God showing favor to Abel's animal offering (Genesis 4:3-5). This practice continued with Noah, who built an altar and offered burnt offerings of clean animals after the flood (Genesis 8:20). The provision of food by God from plants and trees (Genesis 1:29) and the clothing of Adam and Eve with coats of skins (Genesis 3:21) underscore the foundational role of sacrifice in God's relationship with humanity. These passages highlight the significance of obedience, the type of offering, and God's acceptance, setting the stage for understanding sacrifices as acts of worship and devotion.
